trial_court: Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Sindagi, R.A. No.8/2018
case_name: Buddavva W/O Shivappa Talawar vs Shantappa S/O Bhimappa Talawar
facts_of_case: Suit instituted for partition and separate possession by Buddavva seeking ½ share in suit property. Defendant disputed the status of the plaintiff that she is the daughter of Bheemappa born to Sabawwa.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the plaintiff to prove that Gangawwa had died and after her death, Bheemappa got married to Sabawwa.
legal_principles.held: The burden was on the plaintiff to prove that Gangawwa had died and after the demise of Gangawwa, Bheemappa got married to Sabawwa.
cited_cases: Revanasiddappa and another vs. Mallikarjun (2024) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: A child born from a void or voidable marriage is conferred with legitimacy, and such a child has rights to the property of the parents.
legal_principles.held: While conferring legitimacy in terms of sub-section (1) on a child born from a void marriage and under sub-section (2) to a child born from a voidable marriage which has been annulled, the legislature has stipulated that such a child will have rights to or in the property of the parents and not in the property of any other person;
cited_cases: Revanasiddappa and another vs. Mallikarjun (2024) X SCC Y

outcome.final_order: The First Appellate Court allowed the appeal of the plaintiff in part by modifying judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court.

use_for_drafting: modifying judgment and decree in family property disputes
